issues.description: Method Pneumatic.raisePressure(int): The UML in problem_statement.md (UML interface declaration) specifies raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) with return type void, while the solution implementation in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java declares boolean raisePressure(int pressureIncrease). This return-type mismatch between the exercise specification and the provided implementation will confuse students about which signature to implement and may cause compilation/test failures depending on which artifact (UML or implementation/tests) they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface signature consistent with the UML/problem statement. Prefer changing the solution interface to match the UML: in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java replace 'boolean raisePressure(int pressureIncrease);' with 'void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease);' and update any dependent tests or callers accordingly. Alternatively, if the boolean return is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to document 'boolean raisePressure(int)' and explain the semantic meaning of the return value.
